equation_summary: Per token (naive.py:57-71): evolving diagonal metric A in R^K: A <- exp(g_atk_t) * A + beta_atk_t * k_t^2; nonlinear preconditioner M = exp(-log(x)*s) with s = (log(A+eps)-center)/(1+|log(A+eps)-center|); k_precond = k_t * M; then a channel-decayed delta: S <- S * exp(g_t) with g_t in R^K per-channel log decay; S <- S + (beta_t * k_precond) ⊗ (v_t - k_t^T S_decayed); o_t = (scale*q_t)^T S. This is KDA (028) whose write key is modulated by the ATK nonlinear metric — memory plus evolving metric, with retrieval still using the raw k. Separate initial S and A; both returned as final state (naive.py:47-53,73-75).
state_shape: [B,H,K,V] matrix S plus [B,H,K] diagonal metric A
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM call graph E[QKV/KDA gates/ATK parameters] ; B[K2 channel-decayed delta+evolving metric] ; E[output]: inner law is exactly KDA's channel-decayed delta (naive.py:69-71) with the write key replaced by k*M(A) from the ATK recurrence (naive.py:61-67).

CONFIRM 'Metric and channel gates kept distinct; no PGDN name alias': PKDA's S-decay g is per-K-CHANNEL (naive.py:15,69) where PGDN's is per-head scalar, and PKDA retrieval uses k while the write uses k_precond — distinct row, distinct gates.
CONFIRM state-dependent coefficient blocker: M is a nonlinear function of running A, so the transition is not affine; metric VJP must flow through log/squash/exp (naive.py:63-66).
direction_justification: PKDA combines KDA with the same architecture-specific nonlinear ATK preconditioner as PGDN; the nonlinear state-dependent write coefficient does not transfer beyond this two-member family and cannot share the closed linear-delta law, so it stays external.
open_questions: Whether the shared ATK preconditioner across PGDN/PKDA ever justifies a closed two-client descriptor (diagonal metric + monotone squash on write key) — would need a two-client admission record and measured regime; currently kept external.
Whether the KDA inner law with k_precond write / k retrieval asymmetry has any other (even hypothetical) client.
